variants.name: Abstract node base with a virtual child accessor (classic)
variants.idiom_name: abstract Node base with virtual children() + concrete node classes
variants.implementation_notes: The classic C++ realization derives every node kind from an abstract base whose virtual children() accessor returns the normalized child view; concrete classes own their node-specific members (unique_ptr children, operator token, literal value) and implement children() in one place, so no constructor can forget to register a child. Keep the accessor returning a cheap view (span, iterator or cached vector) because it is called once per node per pass.
pitfalls: Returning a freshly allocated std::vector from children() allocates on every visit; return a span or cache the vector for hot walks.
Mixing owning (unique_ptr) and borrowed (raw) child references propagates lifetime bugs - a visitor that outlives the tree must not retain raw Node* from children().
A node that forgets to override children() (or returns an empty list) silently hides its subtree from every generic pass.

variants.name: std::variant node alternatives with std::visit dispatch
variants.idiom_name: std::variant of node structs + std::visit child accessor
variants.implementation_notes: From C++17 the node set can be a variant over small structs that hold their named fields by value, with recursion supplied by a pointer wrapper or an arena index; children() becomes a std::visit over an overload set whose return value is the normalized child view. Choose it when the AST is mostly data and passes are free functions; the virtual class hierarchy remains better when nodes carry stateful behaviour or protected invariants.
pitfalls: A recursive variant must indirect through a pointer or arena index: a variant containing itself by value does not compile.
std::visit demands an exhaustive overload set; a generic catch-all lambda swallows newly added alternatives instead of failing the build.

variants.name: Class hierarchy with a hand-rolled Kind discriminator (LLVM-style RTTI)
variants.implementation_notes: Large production compilers avoid dynamic_cast: an enum Kind in the base plus a static classof() per concrete node makes isa<>/dyn_cast<> cheap and works even for classes without vtables, while the child list is exposed through a uniform iterator pair or a visitor callback. Choose it for very large closed node hierarchies where RTTI cost or vtable layout matters; it keeps the normalized child access while trading standard reflection for a discriminator.
pitfalls: The Kind discriminator must be initialised by every subclass constructor; a missed initialisation makes classof() misclassify nodes and cast them to the wrong type.
Hand-rolled RTTI is a convention, not a language guarantee: a new node type that forgets its classof overload fails silently at every isa<> call site.
Child iterators that expose internal storage must not be invalidated by the traversal itself - rewrites need an explicit two-phase (collect, then mutate) discipline.
